name: monolithic
context: Traditional single-tier software architecture where all components are packaged into a single deployable unit with shared memory space and single database
benefits: Single deployment unit simplifies operations and reduces coordination overhead
In-memory function calls provide lowest latency (nanoseconds vs milliseconds for network calls)
ACID transactions across modules ensure strong data consistency without distributed complexity
Full call stack visibility makes debugging straightforward across all layers
In-process testing enables simpler mocks and faster test execution
No network serialization overhead for internal calls
tradeoffs: Scalability constrained: must scale entire application even if only one component is stressed
Deployment coupling: any code change requires full redeployment of the entire application
Technology lock-in: all components must use the same language, framework, and library versions
Team coordination bottleneck: all teams work in the same codebase, creating merge conflicts
Reliability fragility: failure in any module crashes the entire process
Maintainability decline: codebase complexity grows as the system scales
use_cases: Validating market fit with rapid iteration cycles
Applications with predictable, uniform load patterns
Teams new to distributed systems architecture
Limited budget for DevOps infrastructure and tooling
avoid_when: Team size exceeds 15-20 developers requiring parallel work
Traffic patterns require selective scaling of specific components
Domain complexity requires independent domain model evolution
Technology diversity needed across functional areas
Deployment frequency requirements exceed once per month
Individual component failure should not cascade
component_types: Presentation Layer: REST API, GraphQL resolvers, web UI components, handling HTTP requests and response formatting
Business Logic Layer: Domain services, business rules, workflow orchestration, transaction management
Data Access Layer: Repositories, ORMs, database connections, caching integration
Shared Database: Single relational database (PostgreSQL, MySQL) containing all domain data
anti_patterns: Distributed monolith (services that cannot deploy independently)
Premature decomposition (splitting by technical layer instead of domain)
Big bang rewrite (complete replacement without incremental validation)
Deep module coupling without clear domain boundaries
design_principles: Single Responsibility: Each module should have a single, well-defined purpose within the bounded context
Modularity: Enforce internal module boundaries to prepare for future extraction
Strong Consistency: Leverage ACID transactions for data integrity across modules
In-Memory Communication: Prefer direct function calls over network boundaries for internal operations
Operational Simplicity: Design for single-unit deployment with straightforward rollback and monitoring
Domain-Driven Boundaries: Apply DDD principles within the monolith to identify natural seams before extraction
Interface Stability: Define stable interfaces between modules to enable future independent deployment
best_practices: Operational Simplicity: Single deployment artifact simplifies CI/CD pipelines, one database to backup/monitor/tune, straightforward rollback procedures
Performance Optimization: In-memory function calls achieve nanosecond latency, no network serialization overhead, optimal CPU cache utilization with shared memory
Consistency Guarantees: ACID transactions across all modules, no distributed state synchronization challenges, immediate read-your-writes consistency
Debugging and Observability: Full call stack visible in single process, stack traces don't span network boundaries, simpler profiling and performance analysis
Modular Monolith First: Enforce module boundaries with clear interfaces within a single deployable before committing to microservices
